title: Crosswind Launch Cadence Dashboard and KPI Pulse
content:
Purpose: A compact, operationally focused tracker to run the next 10-week phased rollout for Crosswind (new routing + batching defaults). This doc blends a live KPI scoreboard, a weekly sprint cadence checklist, explicit go/no-go gates, and concrete contingency triggers. Use this for day-to-day ops decisions during the pilot ramp and handoff to steady-state ops.

How to use:
- Daily: Product Ops owns the top-line KPI check at 9:00am PST and posts to #launch-crosswind in Slack.
- Weekly: Owners update their KPI rows by Monday 12:00pm; review during the Tuesday readiness sync.
- Gate decisions: See Rollout Gate Logic section. Decisions must include metric snapshot, root-cause hypothesis, and owner-proposed remediation.

SUMMARY TIMELINE (high level):
- Week 0 (pilot prep): infra capacity verification, canary config, small test cohort.
- Week 1-2 (pilot A): 1% traffic (internal + beta users), baseline metrics collected.
- Week 3-4 (pilot B): 5% traffic, error mode soak and latency stress.
- Week 5-7 (phased ramp): 20% -> 50% based on gated checks.
- Week 8-10 (scale + monitor): 100% traffic and handoff to platform SRE.

KPI TRACKER (current snapshot):
Columns: KPI | Baseline | Current | Target (end of ramp) | Owner | Cadence | Gate Thresholds
- Token throughput (req/sec): 120 | 145 | 400 | Platform Eng | daily | drop >25%
- 95th latency (generation ms): 520ms | 480ms | <=350ms | Serving Runtime | daily | increase >20%
- Error rate (5xx + model-fallback %): 0.6% | 0.9% | <0.5% | SRE | hourly | >1.5% triggers rollback possibility
- Cost per 1k tokens (USD): 0.82 | 0.78 | <=0.55 | Finance/Product | weekly | >+20% vs projected
- Activation conversion (first-call success fraction): 72% | 69% | >=80% | Product-Hosted API | daily | <65% blocks ramp
- Retention (7d after rollout): N/A | N/A | 12% uplift target | Growth | weekly | failure to show expected signal delays expansion
- Regression alerts (eval set failure rate): 0.0% | 1.2% | 0% (zero tolerance) | Applied ML | per-deploy | any >0% -> immediate hold

ROLLING READINESS CHECKLIST (to be completed before each ramp step):
- Infra & Capacity: GPU pool headroom validated (owner: Platform Eng, ticket INF-2789).
- Canaries: Internal canary run 2x expected QPS for 30m without >0.5% errors.
- Observability: Dashboards wired, alert channels set (#alerts-crosswind to page on-call).
- Security & Compliance: No new data flows; signed off by Security (ok-existing KMS).
- Cost Guardrails: Spending limits created and linked to billing alerts.
- Docs & Runbooks: Quick rollback steps, config toggles, and feature-flag owners listed.
- Customer comms: Beta cohort notified; CS briefing completed.

LAUNCH DAY GUARDRAILS (immediate checks for gateway of each phase):
- Gate A (Pilot -> small public): error rate <=1.0% sustained for 48h, 95th latency stable or improving, rollout automation healthy.
- Gate B (small -> mid ramp): cost per 1k tokens not exceeding forecast by >10% for 72h, activation conversion stable.
- Gate C (mid -> full): SRE escalation rate < 1/day and regression evals show no quality drop.

Gating LOGIC (example):
If (error_rate_rolling_6h > gate_threshold) OR (latency_95th increases by >20% vs baseline) then:
  - Pause automated ramp.
  - Run immediate rollback checklist (toggle FF -> previous config).
  - Assign incident owner and run RCA within 8 hours.
  - Notify stakeholders in #launch-crosswind and page on-call.

OWNER ROSTER & RESPONSIBILITIES:
- Product Ops (Ava Martinez): daily cadence, cross-team coordination, exec summaries.
- Serving Runtime (Zoe Chen): latency investigations, perf optimizations, kernel rollout.
- Platform Eng (Ravi Patel): capacity, autoscaling policy, GPU scheduling.
- SRE (Marco Alvarez): alerting, on-call rotations, rollback authority.
- Applied ML (Priya Singh): eval runs, quality regression analysis.
- Growth (TBD): post-launch cohort analysis and retention signals.

CONTINGENCY PLAYS (rank-ordered):
1) Soft-fallback to compatible model variant (configurable via router) — low friction, maintain UX.
2) Temporarily restrict feature to logged-in users or beta cohort only.
3) Throttle batch size / reduce max_tokens to lower cost and exposure.
4) Rollback routing to previous stable environment (hard rollback).

COMMUNICATION TEMPLATES (copy + paste):
- Public beta update: "Crosswind: rolling to 5% traffic today. Monitoring latency and error signals closely; reach out in #launch-crosswind for anomalies."
- Incident open: "INCIDENT: Crosswind #<ticket>. Summary: increased 95th latency. Current status: mitigation in progress. Owner: <name>. ETA for update: 30m."

METRIC COLLECTION & EVALS:
- Eval harness: nightly regression tests using the canonical prompt set (linked GITHUB:pull/3312). Any new failure -> immediate block.
- Token-level cost attribution: Finance will post weekly report to the tracker and flag anomalies >10%.

WEEKLY CADENCE (ops rhythm):
- Monday 12:00pm: KPI row updates due.
- Tuesday 10:00am: Readiness sync (15–30m) — decision node for next step.
- Thursday 3:00pm: Deep-dive (optional) for anomalies.
- Friday EOD: Executive update (1 paragraph + top 2 risks).

DECISION DOCUMENT TEMPLATE (for any go/no-go):
- Decision: advance/pause/rollback
- Snapshot: key metrics (last 72h)
- Hypothesis: likely cause
- Mitigation plan: immediate actions + 24h plan
- Owner & comms: owner + who posts updates

OPEN QUESTIONS & ACTIONS (short list):
- Growth owner to confirm retention KPI baseline and measurement window (action: Growth to assign by 2025-01-22).
- Validate that billing alerts are granular to model variants (action: Finance + Platform by 2025-01-18).
- Confirm runbook steps for model fallback toggle (action: Serving Runtime by 2025-01-20).

APPENDIX: QUICK CHECK - Launch knobs and toggles
- Feature flag: crosswind-routing-v2 (owner: Product Ops)
- Router fallback: model_variant_stable_v3 -> model_variant_stable_v2
- Autoscaling policy: conservative-3x-burst (owner: Platform Eng)

Notes: Keep this doc as the single source of truth for operational decisions during the ramp. Add postmortems and a short ‘lessons learned’ summary after Week 10.
